summary: Matthias Christian Sprengel (1746–1803) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at Rostock, Bützow, and Göttingen under August Ludwig von Schlözer, later holding posts at Göttingen, as librarian at Halle, and at Halle-Wittenberg.

Matthias Hermanns (1899–1972) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Missionshaus St. Gabriel, Vienna under Wilhelm Schmidt and Wilhelm Koppers, and earned a PhD at Fribourg, later teaching at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and Steyler Missionswissenschaftliches Institut.
Matthias de Vries (1820–1892) was a linguist who studied at Leiden University. He served on the faculty at the University of Groningen (1849–1853) and Leiden University (1853–1891).

Matthias von Lexer (1830–1892) specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Graz, Vienna, Berlin, and Erlangen-Nuremberg under scholars including Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, later serving as professor at Freiburg, Würzburg, and Munich.

Matthieu Ricard (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a doctorate in molecular biology under François Jacob at the Pasteur Institute, studied under Kangyur Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and served at Shechen Monastery.

Mattia Salvini is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski and held posts at the International Buddhist College and Mahidol University.

Mauli Chand Prasad worked in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He completed his doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna, and served as Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).
Maureen L. P. Patterson (1930–2019) was an Indology scholar who studied under W. Norman Brown. She served as South Asia Librarian at the University of Chicago (attested 1984 and 2007).

Maurice Bloomfield (1855–1928) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Chicago, Furman, Yale, and Johns Hopkins under Charles Rockwell Lanman, as well as in Germany, before serving as a professor at Johns Hopkins from 1881 to 1926.

Maurice Grammont (1866–1946) was a French linguist who studied at the EPHE and Paris under Ferdinand de Saussure and Michel Bréal. He held posts at the University of Burgundy and as Professor of Comparative Linguistics at Montpellier.
Maurice Jametel (1856–1889) was a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes and later held a post there from around 1886 to 1889.
Maurice Lehot (d. 1931) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon under Félix Lacôte. He worked as a schoolteacher at the Lycée d'Aix-en-Provence.

Maurice Leroy (1909–1990) was a linguist who studied at Université libre de Bruxelles and the EPHE under Vendryes and Benveniste. He became a professor at Bruxelles in 1945 and served as Secrétaire perpétuel of the Royal Belgian Academy.

Maurice O'Connell Walshe (1911–1998) worked in Buddhist studies and linguistics. After studying at UCL, Berlin, Göttingen, and Vienna, he taught German at UCL, Leeds, Nottingham, and Bedford College, and served as Deputy Director at the University of London.

Maurice Phillips (1839–1910) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Bedford College and the University of Bern, served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society (1862–1908), and was a Fellow at the University of Madras.
Maurice Wiles (1923–2005) was a religious studies scholar who was educated at Tonbridge School and Christ's College, Cambridge.
Maurice Wilmotte (1861–1942) was a linguist. He studied at the University of Liège from around 1878 to 1882 and held a post there from circa 1895 to 1931.

Maurine Stuart (1922–1990) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Manitoba and trained under teachers including Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani and Soen Nakagawa. She became president and spiritual director of the Cambridge Buddhist Association in 1979.

Maurizio Taddei (1936–2000) was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Sapienza University under Mario Bussagli, worked at the Museo Nazionale d'Arte Orientale, and taught at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and the Italian Institute for Africa and the East.

Maurizio Tosi (1944–2017) was an archaeologist who studied at Sapienza University of Rome from around 1962 to 1967. He later held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and the University of Bologna.
